B_identity_connection.entry: ConsoleResearchService(pool=existing_async_pool, public_keys_by_id=trusted_backend_keys, organization=approved_org_id, workspace=approved_workspace_id, policies=approved_server_contracts, reader=existing_foundation_reader, enabled=True, environment='dev', issuer=existing_issuer).ask(existing_console_bearer_token, question, private_save_sink)
B_identity_connection.trust_boundary: Constructor arguments are trusted backend composition, never request/model fields. ask does not accept user ID, role, organization, workspace or grants. A caller-written ConsolePrincipal is not accepted instead of a signed token.
checks: Existing verify_console_access_token verifies signature, issuer, subject/user_id equality, type and expiry with zero leeway on every resolution.

A Telchi-local repository reads current user -> workspace -> organization plus active organization membership. Missing/inactive identity, membership, organization or mismatching configured destination deny access.
Signed workspace claims, when present, must match the backend destination.

Password-authenticated tokens reuse ConsoleLoginRepository.session_active and require the existing amr=['pwd'] and integer credential_version contract. Disabled/re-enrolled password sessions cannot retain access. Non-password Console tokens retain their existing expiry/identity contract; no new token-revocation registry is invented.

The backend event loop owns the existing async pool. One worker hosts the unchanged Session/controller; synchronous checks schedule fresh authorization on the backend loop with bounded waits. No cached initial RBAC snapshot is used as ongoing authority.
Only the final authorized business_answer/clarification fields are presentation fields. Raw model prose and reports are private audit material, not verified business answers.
The private save sink may receive in-progress evidence; it is explicitly not a streaming response callback. Authorization loss scrubs the latest presentation report, not the historical server audit.
B_identity_connection.audit: STARTED/completion/BLOCKED events use existing core_events with actor, workspace, investigation UUID and minimal DEV state. Tokens, questions, SQL and commercial values are not added to PG authorization audit. Required audit failures prevent delivery. Repository SQL is implemented but not executed against real PostgreSQL in this window.
B_identity_connection.timeouts_and_cleanup: Authorization and audit each have a 10-second async deadline; worker reauthorization waits at most 10 seconds. SQL/model/host budgets remain existing. Cancellation sets the existing event, waits for worker cleanup and closes its binding, including a cancellation received while discovery was pending. Foundation attachment remains non-preemptible as previously documented.

C_effective_permissions.resolver: Unmodified PermissionConsoleRepository.list_effective_permissions; existing roles, permission profiles and scoped FULL_ACCESS expansion remain authoritative.
C_effective_permissions.scope_intersection: Resolved grants are intersected with enabled core_workspace_capabilities for module telchi and its permission namespace. Technical permissions do not become business access. SourcePolicy then intersects organization, workspace, whole-dataset attestation and approved columns.
C_effective_permissions.full_access: No special treatment of the FULL_ACCESS string or Presidencia role. Existing resolver expands only active scoped grants within its organization/workspace/module semantics. This bridge does not duplicate that expansion.
C_effective_permissions.presidencia: BLOCKED: Mario and Abraham's actual identities and effective business grants were NOT queried or compared. Equality must not be inferred from the broad-scope fixture or previous reports. No technical permissions were granted to either.

limitations: Reader-unsupported datasets remain explicit gaps; no direct physical Foundation paths or SAP/HANA fallback.
Structural discovery is not semantic accreditation. Dynamically discovered tables currently have no accredited grain/measure contracts or relationships in the issued catalog.
SourcePolicy is an approved server-side data contract, not evidence that an existing capability permission automatically grants exploratory access to every row/column of its source.
There are no default broad policies. Concrete permission-to-source/column/whole-row contracts still require approval and composition; this phase does not arbitrarily define pending business policy.

demonstrated: Signed identity fixtures, actual PASETO verification and the same Session/AST/executor execute a derived CTE aggregation against a small READ_ONLY DuckDB fixture.
Under a restricted effective scope the model stub receives sales_line without private_note and without any inventory dataset metadata. A prompt claiming Presidencia cannot expand it.

Under the broader fixture the identical investigator exposes inventory too; the model stub selects that newly visible source and executes a different aggregation. Actual SQL results are 30 for fixture sales and 7 for fixture inventory. These are synthetic test values, not Telchi business facts.

Existing tests cover forbidden datasets/columns through direct SQL, CTEs, subqueries, aggregations and joins; copied contexts, tenant/workspace changes, stale snapshots and old observations are denied.
New service test revokes access after a completed query and completion audit, before return: delivery fails closed and the saved presentation is blank.
Existing test revokes during the model call and clears session history. Backend authorization outages cannot reuse cached authority.
Partial-row scopes remain excluded; no unsafe row-policy emulation was introduced.

This is not a real Luna trace, actual FULL_ACCESS database expansion or productive authorization. In-process SourcePolicy changes require closing/reissuing a binding. Persistent cross-investigation resume remains disabled.
